title: A Veil for the Choir
premise: Isandro Reyes has survived the Thornfell mountains by being nobody: a beast-speaker who hides their gift even from the smugglers they guide, trading silence for safety. But when a scholar's stolen prophecy book names them by an old family name and foretells the death of the mountain's buried court, Isandro learns their grandmother sold her own soul to that court a century ago to end a famine—and the debt has come due, payable now in Isandro's blood or their voice. To break the contract, Isandro must lead a ragged band—prophecy-scholar Wren, the court's exiled half-fae herald Cael, and the beasts who alone know the deep roads—beneath the mountain to steal the soul back before the first long winter snow seals the gates. They succeed only by giving up the thing they guarded most: Isandro speaks their gift aloud to the court, shattering the veil of invisibility, and chooses love with Cael over the anonymity that once kept them alive.
about_author: Astrid Delacroix is the pen name of a former alpine trail guide who spent six winters mapping smugglers' paths across the Pyrenees before turning to fantasy. They write about borders—geographic, magical, and personal—from a stone farmhouse where the sheep, they insist, answer back.

chapters.title: The Quiet Toll
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A routine smuggling run through Thornfell goes wrong when Isandro's beasts warn of an ambush, forcing them to use their forbidden gift openly for the first time in years to save their clients. The emotional beat is dread: one witness saw too much, and Isandro realizes invisibility is a debt always coming due.

chapters.title: A Book Bound in Birchbark
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, a disgraced prophecy scholar fleeing the capital, shows Isandro a century-old text naming 'the Reyes who speaks' as the one who will unmake the mountain court. Isandro denies everything, but the prophecy's final line—the long winter finishes falling tonight—begins as frost creeps down the valley. Beat: denial cracking into fear.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Buried
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Searching their late grandmother's cabin, Isandro finds a contract sealed in ash: her soul sold to the court beneath the mountain to end the famine of 1823, with the debt transferable down the bloodline. The beasts refuse to enter the low passes, whining at the dark. Beat: grief curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: The Herald in the Snowline
chapters.summary: Cael's POV. Cael, the court's exiled herald, intercepts the party to deliver the summons: the court will accept Isandro's voice in place of their blood. Haunted by centuries of carrying death warrants, Cael offers instead to guide them through the gates he once guarded. Beat: wary alliance; the first spark of something warmer.

chapters.title: Toll Roads and Old Debts
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The party descends through smuggler roads Isandro alone knows, bartering passage with river-trolls and bribing a bridge-wight with a true name. Wren deciphers that the court feeds on remembered souls; the famine was its last feeding. Beat: rising tension as the winter snow begins to seal the passes behind them.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Cael's POV. The party enters the court's cathedral cavern, where the sold souls hang like lanterns—Isandro's grandmother among them, still singing. The court's magister offers Isandro a bargain: their voice freely given, and all debts end. Isandro nearly accepts. Beat: temptation, and Cael's quiet horror at watching them consider it.

chapters.title: A Theft of Lanterns
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The heist: while Cael distracts the court with a herald's formal challenge, Isandro and Wren steal the soul-lanterns, guided by the beasts who have tunneled their own way down. The alarm sounds as the grandmother's lantern flickers toward Isandro's hand. Beat: desperate, breathless momentum.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Finishes Falling
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The gates begin to seal with the first snow; Wren is caught, and the court demands a soul in exchange for her life. Isandro realizes the prophecy's true meaning: not that they die, but that they stop hiding. They speak their gift aloud before the whole court, commanding the mountain's stone itself. Beat: sacrifice transformed into claim.

chapters.title: Every Voice at Once
chapters.summary: Cael's POV. Isandro's spoken gift shatters the court's claim over all the lantern-souls; the grandmother's spirit chooses, at last, to pass on, thanking Isandro in a voice like thaw. The court, starving without its harvest, offers Cael his old throne back. He refuses it. Beat: catharsis, grief, and choice.

chapters.title: A Veil, Lifted
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Above ground, the long winter breaks early; the party emerges to a valley that knows Isandro's name and, surprisingly, doesn't fear it. Isandro and Cael choose each other over the old safety of anonymity, and Isandro takes work guiding openly—with beasts at their side and nothing left to hide. Beat: hard-won peace, love chosen against duty's ghost.
